angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 502,295 km at 100.96 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.9052 +/- 0.0227 mas (same row, RUWE 1.22): 100.96 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.722 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Alsubai et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Qatar-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155...52A/abstract): 502,295 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.822 +/- 0.021 solar masses from Alsubai et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Qatar-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155...52A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5052 +/- 66 K from Alsubai et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Qatar-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155...52A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Alsubai et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Qatar-6 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155...52A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/qatar-6.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.636, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
